newsitem.title: INDIA: Delhi stocks end up on political developments.
newsitem.headline: Delhi stocks end up on political developments.

text.p: Late buying by speculators, coupled with short covering by brokers, lifted Delhi stock prices to close higher on Friday, prompted by fresh political developments, brokers said.

Traders said the session was mostly speculative, on reports that top United Front leaders were meeting to find ways to rescue the government ahead of the trust vote, scheduled for 2000 hours (1430 GMT).
The benchmark Delhi Stock Exchange sensitive index bounced back to close 11.24 points higher at 761.74 points, after dropping to 738.36 points in early trade.

"The recovery seems to be temporary due to large-scale buying by speculators and domestic financial houses. The outcome of today's confidence vote will decide the fate of the market," said Manoj Choraria of stockbrokers Choraria Investments.

Shares of Reliance Industries were traded heavily on speculators' activity throughout the session and finally ended 3.10 rupees higher at 269.10 rupees on late buying, after dipping to 256.40 rupees at the outset of the session.
TISCO ended two rupees up at 165.50 rupees, following the revival of speculative buying towards the end of the session.

Shares of the State Bank of India, the largest public-sector banking company, gained 3.45 rupees to 278 rupees on buying by some domestic financial houses, after dropping to 263 rupees on panic-selling by FIIs early in the session.
Cement-maker ACC firmed up 45 rupees to 1,390 rupees on massive speculative buying followed by shortcovering.
ITC Ltd made a notable rally towards the close of session on huge short-covering by bear operators and ended 17.45 rupees up at 398.65 rupees after dropping to 368 on nervous offerings.
Hindustan Lever rose five rupees to 1,025 rupees while SmithKline Beecham Consumer rose two rupees to 292 on low-level buying.

TELCO rose 2.20 rupees to 393 rupees, BSES Ltd rose 5.50 to 225 rupees, MTNL rose 10 rupees to 278 rupees, Apollo Tyres rose 5.50 rupees to 116.40 rupees and Brooke Bond Lipton five rupees to 445 rupees.
